title: A Case Study by Using Khan Academy, an Open-Source Environment
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a flipped-classroom approach supported by Khan Academy and mathematics software can improve the teaching and learning of Grade 10 mathematics, specifically the topic of functions. The authors also ask how students perceive this learning model and its supporting tools. The study is positioned as relevant to implementation of technology-supported instruction in Vietnam, especially in the context of increased online learning during the Covid-19 period.

The intervention combined Khan Academy’s free learning platform with Desmos in a flipped format. Students first used Khan Academy at home to watch short instructional videos and complete practice exercises, then used class time for checking work, discussion, teacher feedback, and collaborative problem-solving with software support. The study involved 20 Grade 10 students at a private school in Hanoi, Vietnam, over four weeks. Data came from both quantitative and qualitative sources, including a survey of student and teacher experiences and classroom observation/analysis.

The authors report that the flipped model improved students’ understanding of mathematical functions, made concepts more visual and concrete, and helped students come to class better prepared. Students also felt the approach supported retention and reduced rote memorization. At the same time, the paper notes practical constraints: some students had difficulty using computers or mathematics software, and teachers needed to prepare additional instructional resources to integrate Khan Academy effectively into the classroom. Overall, the paper concludes that the approach was promising for mathematics learning in this setting, but it requires adequate digital readiness and teacher-supported implementation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small single-group case study with qualitative and descriptive quantitative data, not a controlled comparison. It provides useful implementation insights, but the evidence base is limited by lack of randomization, no control group, and reliance on self-report and survey frequencies.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported impact appears positive but is modest and unsupported by a rigorous effect estimate. The study suggests promising implementation conditions for a priority K-12 population, but the small sample and single-site design make the generalizable impact unclear.

interventions.use_case: Khan Academy used in a flipped-classroom mathematics unit for grade 10 students, with video lessons, practice exercises, personalized dashboard, mastery tracking, and teacher monitoring.
Desmos used as supporting classroom software for in-class graphing and visualization during the flipped mathematics lessons.

finding.finding_summary: The study reports that the flipped-classroom approach using Khan Academy boosted student achievement in mathematics for 20 grade 10 students over 4 weeks. The paper does not provide a standardized test effect size, but it describes improved understanding of functions, better problem solving, and stronger performance on class assessments and exercises.
finding.measure: Mathematics achievement in functions unit; class assessments, exercises, and student reports of understanding

finding.finding_summary: The paper suggests gains in metacognition and collaborative learning conditions: students used self-assessment via Khan Academy dashboards and worked in peer groups during class. These features were reported to help students identify strengths and weaknesses, come to class prepared, discuss concepts, and develop more conceptual understanding.
finding.measure: Self-assessment use, classroom collaboration, and student-reported preparedness/metacognition

finding.finding_summary: Student survey responses were strongly positive, with 90% reporting enhanced understanding, 60% reporting better visualization and retention, and 20% reporting increased motivation. Some students also reported reduced fear of difficult function problems and greater confidence in learning the topic.
finding.measure: Student survey on perceptions, motivation, and confidence

finding.finding_summary: The paper indicates that teacher dashboards and assignment reports helped teachers monitor student progress, check time on task, and adapt teaching plans. This is presented as improving instructional management rather than as a formally measured workload effect.
finding.measure: Teacher dashboard monitoring and assignment reporting
